findings.finding: F1 (blocking): A2's greps can pass while the convention survives, because envoy.ts hands Fence across function boundaries (:1070, :1750, :2049, :2261, :2429, :2488, :2536, :2798, :2915, :2965) and carries a second hand-written guard neither grep names, const stillHolds (:2270, checked :2283, :2290). A2's third clause depends on a state list that did not exist.
findings.answer: The queue hands a handle object, not a function; Fence, UNFENCED and serialQueue all leave envoy.ts. stillHolds becomes a precondition inside the module's own reassertRole operation. Plan section 1 F1 fixes the three exact grep commands A2 becomes, including the identifier grep over the state list of section 2. No permanent grep check is committed: the structure is the enforcement (STRATEGY.md, 'Climb the enforcement ladder only as far as needed').

findings.finding: F2 (blocking): the module/envoy.ts state boundary was undrawn, and A2 pins sessionOpen's definition to envoy.ts (:2159) while it reads sessionID (:719) and hostSessionID() (:2155).
findings.answer: Plan section 2 fixes the partition. sessionID, sessionDirectory, subscriptions, connection, heartbeatRegistered, announced, continues, recordedSessionKey, notifiedSessions and lastHeard stay in envoy.ts; the module takes sessionOpen as an injected predicate and imports no Oh My Pi host type, taking an EnvoyClient, sessionOpen, deadlineMs, notify, log, appendRoleClaimEntry and two NATS adapters. sessionID's write inside a pass (:2806) is synchronous before the first await, so no fence reaches it.

findings.finding: F3 (blocking): when a handle's session is bound was unspecified; reconcileNow learns its session inside the task (:2800) and reconcile queues with no id (:2787).
findings.answer: run takes no session. The handle starts unbound; a task binds it once with handle.actFor(id). An unbound handle is guarded by the deadline alone (A1's no-session task). Binding twice throws. Plan section 1 F3 names the binding of each of the four queued entry points (:2787, :2878, :3108, :4047).

findings.finding: F4 (blocking): 'refused step ends the task as decided nothing' collides with today's AbandonedTaskError, which the heartbeat reads as its stall signal (:2406-2410) and settleRole catches (:3036).
findings.answer: Both of today's outcomes are kept, which R4 also requires. Deadline fired: run still rejects with AbandonedTaskError (:296-303), and a step refused after it throws a module-private StepRefused the queue swallows as it swallows a late rejection today. Session moved: the handle refuses, run resolves undefined, and reconcile maps it to false, which is the boolean A1's 'a pass the host leaves mid-pass resolves false' asserts on.

findings.finding: F5 (blocking): user-visible notices are none of R2's four step kinds, yet R4 depends on warnNoticesClosed being suppressed (:3032, writing roleNoticesFor and notifying at :3069-3077).
findings.answer: A notice that reports the result of a state write is part of that write's named operation and fires only when the write lands: warnNoticesClosed (:3069), warnRoleEnded (:3050), the refusal notice in reassertRoleNow (:2301). A notice that reports an outage runs in the heartbeat timer, outside every queued task, and is never swallowed: :2417 and :2355. The division already exists in the code; the plan makes it structural, so no architect decision is needed.

findings.finding: F6 (blocking): mergeForClaim (internal/session/claim.go:29-34) can return the incumbent entry wholesale, so R5's 'a registration replaces the stored id' is not true for a discarded registration.
findings.answer: R5 governs the write the merge accepts; a discarded registration stores nothing, as it stores no other field today. Measured: both clients carrying this change register port 0 and driving false (envoy.ts:2221,2229; envoy-channel-server.ts:744-755), so neither merge rule fires between them. The discard bites only against a portful or driving incumbent, today the OpenCode plugin (envoy-plugin/src/server.ts:93-98), which sends no id, so the claim falls to R6 case 3. T1 adds a test pinning exactly that.

findings.finding: F7 (blocking): roleSetHandler reads the claimant with Get (api.go:1100), which is cache-only (registry.go:371-380), then writes that entry back with PutWithin (:1111) — so a trailing cache reads an empty id and overwrites the bucket's newer one.
findings.answer: Fixed in T2 as a clear defect in code this change touches. The handler keeps Get for its 404/503 answers, then reads the same key through Refresh under roleHolderReadTimeout: on success that entry is the one it refreshes and the one R6 reads the claimant's id from; on any failure it keeps the Get entry, so the result is never worse than today. No instance id is added to the POST /v1/roles/set body: R5 authorises it on registration and deregistration only, and a claimant is always registered by then (:1100-1107).

findings.finding: F8 (blocking): R6's bucket read of the predecessor has no call shape — liveSessionEntry answers from the cache whenever the predicate accepts (role_holder.go:198-205, with `registered` at :227) — and today's predecessor branch does zero reads (api.go:1131-1132), so the route gains cost inside sendRequestBudget.
findings.answer: T2 adds bucketSessionEntry(ctx, sessions, id, bound) beside liveSessionEntry: sessions.Refresh under bound, nothing else. ErrKeyNotFound is R6 case 1, an entry is compared with session.InstanceMatches, any other error is writeBusUnavailable 503, as the holder-liveness error is today (:1135-1136). The route gains two bucket reads, each capped at roleHolderReadTimeout (2 s) inside sendRequestBudget (3.5 s). The machine check that it still fits is the existing frozen-bus route table, cmd/listener/write_routes_frozen_bus_test.go (writeRoutesWithin = 4 s), which already covers /v1/roles/set.

findings.finding: F9 (blocking): R7's revision-conditional delete has no API — SessionRegistry.Delete uses DeleteAtRead and never inspects the value (registry.go:445-483) — and the spec does not say what a lost compare-and-swap answers.
findings.answer: T3 adds (*SessionRegistry).DeleteIfInstance, shaped on store.Registry.deleteInterestAt (store/kv.go:1233-1260) over bus.KeyValue.Delete(key, nats.LastRevision(rev)) (bus/kv.go:182): read value and revision from the bucket, ErrKeyNotFound answers deleted=true, a non-matching InstanceMatches writes nothing and answers deleted=false, otherwise delete at that revision; a lost CAS (nats.ErrKeyExists) retries the whole sequence once, because its common cause is the same instance's own heartbeat and a spurious 'kept' would turn the next claim into a needless 409; a second loss answers deleted=false. The cache is reconciled as Delete reconciles it. A delete with no id keeps calling Delete.

findings.finding: F10 (blocking): restoreRole deletes the predecessor's role record on any refusal (claude-envoy/src/envoy-channel-server.ts:773-776), and the record is keyed by session id in a shared state directory, so a refused process A deletes live process B's file. No R-number owns the fix R8 states in prose.
findings.answer: T5 implements it and settles the case R8 does not name: a 409 whose holder IS the session the claim named as predecessor keeps the file, because that record belongs to the live holder; a 409 naming any other session deletes it, because the predecessor demonstrably no longer holds the role. transferRole (:869-885) needs no separate rule: restoreRole resolves on a refusal, so roleTransferFrom clears and no heartbeat retries, which is the spec's 'No retry after a refusal' decision. reassertRole (:845-848) deletes its own record and is untouched.

findings.finding: F11 (blocking): A3 and A5 have no surface a Legion pod can run. smoke-registration-stall.sh refuses without a live ENVOY_URL and bearer (:38-47), needs a real omp and a real model turn (:261), and scratches in /tmp (:171). The only pod-runnable real-listener surface is envoy-client/test/envoy-stack.ts behind LEGION_E2E_ENVOY_STACK=1.
findings.answer: T8 builds both. A5: packages/pi-envoy/scripts/smoke-role-takeover.sh starts natsd and a listener built from the branch as envoy-stack.ts does, and drives every row of R8's table with separate OS processes — one Bun child per Oh My Pi extension instance loading the real extension against the package's stand-in host, and the real claude-envoy channel-server process for the Claude rows — needing go and bun only, no credential and no model; --base-rev builds the listener from main for the two runs that must fail there. It becomes one step of the existing envoy-session-stall CI job. A3: --local-stack on smoke-registration-stall.sh plus the $TMPDIR fix; its one remaining live need is a model provider for the spawned omp, which the implementer resolves through agent-secrets and, failing that, asks for as a credential only a person can give.

findings.finding: F12 (blocking): dispatch://INFRA-392 published spec v2 after this spec was approved, making the envoy_interests row the durable record and the clean DELETE a stop marker; the 'no design conflict' claim predates it.
findings.answer: Settled directly with INFRA-392's architect (its Envoy message to this planner, 2026-10-30T23:56Z), and allowed by this spec's Design ('Live in R6 means what the registry's liveness rule says when this change merges'): the field is ClientInstanceID with json tag client_instance_id,omitempty on session.SessionEntry, which INFRA-392 copies into its interest row's session sub-record; liveness stays liveSessionEntry here and INFRA-392 moves it onto its new (*SessionRegistry).IsLive; this change writes the shared helper session.InstanceMatches, which INFRA-392 calls against the interest row; whichever pull request merges second rebases. T0 re-reads INFRA-392's live state before T1. Left for the architect: confirm that a predecessor INFRA-392 calls unresponsive is R6 case 1, which is the plan's reading.

findings.answer: A6's grep is kept and run, but section 6 of the plan is what decides R9: one row per text, naming the sentence it must lose and the rule it must state, which the reviewer checks. Two texts outside R9's list are added because they tell a reader a now-false rule: docs/solutions/envoy/heartbeat-role-reassertion-and-regain-hooks.md and docs/solutions/envoy/session-id-remint-stale-transcript-identity.md. docs/plans/2026-09-12-heartbeat-role-reassertion.md is left as human-authored design history, the CHANGELOGs are written by the fold, and packages/envoy-client/AGENTS.md does not exist, which R9's own wording allows for.

findings.finding: F14: A1's 'each named operation leaves the state its name says' is unrunnable until R3's list exists.
findings.answer: Section 3 of the plan is that table: nine named operations and seven read accessors, each with the state it leaves and the code path that calls it today (envoy.ts:2385, :3107, :3155, :3920, :3966, :2381, :3339, :3252, :2694-2705, :3136-3141, :3151, :2560, :2583-2589). A1's last bullet is one test per row.

findings.finding: F15: where the client instance id is minted was not stated, and a module-scope constant in packages/pi-envoy/src/ would be per process, while an ACP host runs several top-level sessions in one process, each with its own extension instance (envoy.ts:617, :871-874; pi-envoy/AGENTS.md:1023).
findings.answer: The id is minted inside the module's factory, which envoyExtension calls once per instance, so it is per extension instance as R5 requires; for claude-envoy it is minted in runEnvoyChannelServer beside the client (:1453), one per process. A plugin reload is a new instance and so a new id, which is right for R8 row 1: that claim runs under the holder's own session id and never reaches the predecessor rule.
